title: KPI Forensics and Capacity Proof Playbook
author: Aisha Patel
body:
Summary
--------
This playbook defines a single-pane process for: (1) classifying SRE KPIs for forensic value, (2) retaining the right telemetry and artifacts for post-incident analysis, and (3) performing capacity-proof checks that bridge SLO enforcement with provisioning decisions. It is intended for oncall responders, SRE owners, and product stewards.

Scope
-----
Applies to all Redwood customer-facing inference services (hosted API, dedicated model pools, private deployments) and to the telemetry streams that feed our SLO and capacity tooling (Prometheus, tracing, request/response logs, KV-cache telemetry). This playbook complements runbooks and tabletop scenarios; it focuses on what to collect, how long to keep it, and how to run reproducible capacity proofs.

Goal and constraints
- Ensure a repeatable evidence trail for all SLO-impacting incidents.
- Keep retention cost bounded: three-tier retention policy (hot, warm, cold) described below.
- Provide automation recipes for rapid evidence collection and capacity proof replays.

KPI taxonomy (for forensic prioritization)
--------------------------------------
We classify KPIs by forensic weight to decide what to capture at incident time. Use this taxonomy when choosing sampling rates and retention tiers.

1) Tier A (Critical forensic KPIs) - always captured at full fidelity for 30 days:
   - SLO error-rate per model route (p99 failure fraction for requests matched to SLO).
   - Tail latency quantiles for generation endpoints (p95, p99, p999).
   - Token-level generation time and KV-cache hit/miss ratios.
   - Request/response traces that include model version, container id, and GPU id.

2) Tier B (High value diagnostic KPIs) - captured at aggregated or sampled fidelity for 90 days:
   - Request size distribution (input tokens), response token counts.
   - App-level error codes and HTTP gateway latencies.
   - Batch sizes and batching delays (if batching enabled).

3) Tier C (Low immediate forensic value) - retained aggregated for 1 year:
   - Hourly capacity utilization per instance type.
   - Model load balancer metrics and node heartbeats.

Evidence retention matrix (text table)
--------------------------------------
Use this matrix to make retention decisions for artifacts collected during incidents.

Artifact | Tier | Retention | Storage location | Retrieval SLA
-------- | ---- | --------- | ---------------- | -------------
Full request+response payload | A | 30d hot | GCS-hot/slo-forensics/ | 5m
Tracing spans (full) | A | 30d hot | Jaeger-hot/ | 5m
KV-cache dumps (periodic) | A | 30d hot + archived weekly | S3://redwood-archives/kv-dumps/ | 1h
Prometheus raw samples (10s) | B | 90d warm | TSDB-cluster/longterm/ | 15m
Aggregated hourly metrics | C | 365d cold | BigQuery:metrics_agg | 4h
System logs (task-level) | B | 90d warm | Fluentd-indexed/ | 30m
Model inference core dumps | A | 90d locked (security) | Artifacts-secured/ | 1h (restricted access)

Retention cost-control rules
- All Tier A artifact storage must be scoped per-incident and auto-archived to cold after 30d unless a reviewer extends retention with documented rationale.
- Tier B artifacts use downsampling after 14 days (10s -> 1m).
- Tier C aggregated datasets can be retained indefinitely but must be compressed and access-controlled.

Operational runbooks (rapid forensic path)
-----------------------------------------
This section describes the canonical steps an oncall uses to collect evidence and evaluate capacity impact.

1) Immediate containment (0-15 minutes):
   1.1) Acknowledge pager and record initial hypothesis.
   1.2) Toggle request-level debug sampling to 100% for the affected route (CLI):
       - kubectl exec -n redwood svc/route-config -- /bin/sh -c 'curl -XPOST http://localhost:8080/debug/sampling?rate=1.0'
   1.3) Mark incident in infra-ticket: tag with model version, region, and SLO id.

2) Evidence capture (15-60 minutes):
   2.1) Pull traces for the last 60 minutes filtered by trace.tag:service=runtime AND trace.tag:model_version=<VERSION>. Example Jaeger query: service=runtime AND tags.model_version=\"v2.3.1\"
   2.2) Export Prometheus raw samples around the spike window (PromQL example):
       - promql: rate(http_requests_total{route=\"/v1/generate\"}[1m])
   2.3) Snapshot the KV-cache hit ratio: curl -H 'Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN' https://internal-api/kvcache/snapshot?pool=warm
   2.4) If memory OOM suspected, copy container core dump: gsutil cp /var/crash/core.<id> gs://redwood-forensics/core-dumps/<incident-id>/

3) Capacity-proof (1-4 hours):
   3.1) Define proof hypothesis: e.g., \"At 80% per-GPU sustained utilization, request latency p99 will exceed 1.2s\".
   3.2) Create a synthetic replay job (k8s job template snippet):
       apiVersion: batch/v1
       kind: Job
       metadata:
         name: capacity-proof-<incident-id>
       spec:
         template:
           spec:
             containers:
             - name: replay
               image: replay-tool:stable
               args: [\"--trace-prefix\", \"gs://redwood-forensics/traces/<incident-id>/\", \"--target-util\", \"0.8\"]
   3.3) Run the job in a shadow namespace against a compatible model variant with pinned weights. Monitor: GPU util, batch latency, p99 latency. Use 'kubectl top' and PromQL dashboards.
   3.4) Record outcome: pass/fail and attach timestamped metrics snapshots to the incident ticket.

Incident review standards (evidence & conclusions)
--------------------------------------------------
- Every incident review must include: the initial hypothesis, who ran the capacity proof, the proof artifacts (replay results + metric snapshots), and a clear remediation decision (capacity increase, retry logic, or model configuration change).
- Use the following evidence scoring rubric (0-5):
   - 0: no reproducible evidence
   - 1-2: weak correlation only
   - 3: moderate correlation, partial replay
   - 4: strong correlation, full replay on canary cluster
   - 5: definitive repro, multiple replay runs consistent
- If score < 3, label the incident as \"investigations_required\" and schedule a dedicated repro lab within 7 business days.

Automation and tooling integrations
---------------------------------
Integrate the following automations into the incident lifecycle to reduce manual toil.

- Telemetry snapshot operator (recommended): periodically exports 10-minute windows of Prometheus, traces, and logs for active incidents to a GCS bucket. Configure with incident label.
- Incident evidence webhook: on ticket creation, trigger a Job that sets sampling=1.0 and starts trace buffering. Example PagerDuty webhook -> internal-runbook-runner.
- Proof orchestration (replay orchestration service): a CI job that can run recorded traces against a pinned model image and produce a reproducible metrics bundle.

PromQL / query examples (operational)
- p99 latency for route /v1/generate over 1m: histogram_quantile(0.99, sum(rate(http_request_duration_seconds_bucket{route=\"/v1/generate\"}[1m])) by (le))
- error rate by model version: sum(rate(http_requests_total{job=\"runtime\",code=~\"5..\"}[5m])) by (model_version) / sum(rate(http_requests_total{job=\"runtime\"}[5m])) by (model_version)

Escalation & ownership matrix
-----------------------------
Role | Responsibility | Pager escalation
-----|---------------|------------------
Service Owner | Interpret SLO impact, approve retention extension | Pager 1
SRE Oncall | Run containment & evidence capture | Pager 0
Platform Capacity Lead | Run capacity proofs, recommend provisioning changes | Pager 2
Model Steward | Confirm model-variant compatibility for replay | Pager 3
SecOps | Unlock access to secured artifacts (core dumps) | Pager 2 (restricted)

Runbook snippets (copy-paste)
----------------------------
1) Toggle sampling (curl):
   curl -XPOST -H 'Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN' https://internal-api/route-config/debug/sampling -d '{"route":"/v1/generate","rate":1.0}'

2) Snapshot Prometheus range to GCS (cli):
   promtool tsdb export --from=$(date -d '1 hour ago' +%s) --to=$(date +%s) --match='job=\"runtime\",route=\"/v1/generate\"' | gsutil cp - gs://redwood-forensics/prom-extracts/<incident-id>.prom

3) Launch capacity-proof (kubectl):
   kubectl apply -f capacity-proof-job.yaml -n replay-namespace

Postmortem template (required fields)
-----------------------------------
- Title, date, incident owner, SLO impacted (IDs)
- Timeline with evidence pointers (GCS URIs, trace IDs)
- Capacity proof summary (commands run, results)
- Evidence score (0-5) and rationale
- Immediate remediation and long-term action items (owner + ETA)
- Retention extension decision (if any) and approver

Appendix: reproducible replay checklist
-------------------------------------
- Lock model binary to exact commit and container image.
- Use same batcher configuration as production or document deviation.
- Recreate KV-cache warm-up sequence prior to replay.
- Replay at multiple concurrency levels (50%, 80%, 100% of masked per-GPU throughput).
- Archive all replay logs and attach to ticket.

FAQ and common gotchas
----------------------
Q: \"Can we extend Tier A retention automatically?\"
A: No. Extensions require a named approver and written rationale to avoid runaway hot storage costs.

Q: \"What if replay is non-deterministic?\"
A: Increase sample count, stabilize RNG seeds in model container, and capture environment differences (CUDA driver, kernel versions).

Q: \"Who can access locked artifacts?\"
A: SecOps grants time-bound access; always request via the incident ticket workflow.
